{"findings":[{"rule_id":"NM-002","evidence":[{"kind":"note","ref":"N1","page":1,"quote":"INDUCTION HARDENED TO BE DONE FOR INDICATED AREA"},{"kind":"note","ref":"N3","page":1,"quote":"HEAT TREATMENT NOTE:- 1) PROFILE CUTTING SHOULD BE DONE. 2) TO BE CASE CARBURISING DONE. 2) TO BE INDUCTION HARDENED UPTO 50 ~ 55 HRC. 3) CASE DEPTH 0.8~ 1.2 mm."}],"comment":"Note N1 restricts induction hardening to an 'indicated area' while note N3 lists both case carburising and induction hardening as blanket heat-treatment steps without defining any indicated area, creating a contradiction that will confuse the heat-treat shop about which surfaces receive which process. The designer should reconcile N1 and N3 by clearly identifying the induction-hardened zone on the drawing or in the notes and removing the duplicate step numbering in N3."
    ,"recommended_correction":"Revise the heat treatment notes so that the scope of induction hardening versus case carburising is unambiguous and consistent across all notes."}]}
